findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkbox tasks, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: Lines 71, 94, 117, 126 and 134 write the commits as `- [ ] **Task 2C: Commit** — ...`. A commit marker must be a plain line, never a checkbox. As checkboxes, task-checker tooling and progress counts treat them as work items. Placement is fine: 2C, 3C and 4C each come right after their test task. Rewrite each one as a plain line, e.g. `**Commit**: feat(core): add slice design heading validator`.

findings.title: Task 5 can commit an untested code fix under a `docs:` message
findings.description: Line 122 tells the implementer to fix any unexplained parity `DIFF` and add a test. Task 5C (line 126) then commits under `docs: record slice 214 parity sweep results`. No step between the fix and that commit rebuilds or reruns the core or CLI tests. The full suite only runs in Task 6 (line 130), after 5C. So a source change can be committed at an untested point, labelled as docs. Fix: after a fix, rerun `pnpm -r build` and the affected package tests, then commit with `fix(core|cli): ...`. Keep the `docs:` commit for the Implementation Notes edit only.

findings.title: Task 5's "intended difference" list is narrower than how `parseFrontmatter` actually behaves, and invites edits to shared code
findings.description:
Line 122 accepts a parity `DIFF` only if it comes from "quoted `docType`, CRLF, `\r`, real heading syntax". Everything else is a bug to fix. But reusing `parseFrontmatter` (design line 90) brings more differences than the quoted value:
- It trims `---` delimiter lines and value lines (line 16, `stripped`).
- It accepts an indented `docType:` outside a nested block.
- It is **stricter** than the script in one case: frontmatter with no closing `---` returns `found: false` (line 62). The script's awk passes it through `END { exit found ? 0 : 1 }` (`project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/validate-slice-design:85`).

Task 2 also implements trimmed-marker comparison (design line 103), which isn't on the list either. A junior agent who hits one of these will "fix" it, and the obvious place is `parseFrontmatter`, which many other features use. Fix:
- List every difference that comes from `parseFrontmatter`.
- Say that any fix goes in `sliceDesignFiles.ts`, never in the shared parser.
- Note that the unclosed-frontmatter case is a strictness regression against SC line 167 if a real file hits it.

findings.title: "Original heading text" is ambiguous; the contract needs the full heading line with its `#`s
findings.description: Task 2 says `RequiredHeading` holds the "original heading text for messages". Task 3 (line 75) says `missing` holds the "original heading text". The design's output, though, is `missing: ## Value` (slice line 120) and `["## Value"]` (line 135), and the SC says "written as in the template" (line 168). The script prints the raw heading line, `$prev` (`validate-slice-design:59`). Read literally, "heading text" means the text after the hashes (`Value`), and that would fail Task 4T line 109 much later. Fix: say "the full template heading line with `\r` stripped, including the `#` prefix and any `{placeholder}`". Add a 2T assertion that `# Slice Design: {slice-name}` keeps its original form.

findings.title: The worktree test may use `--project`, which doesn't check the worktree success criterion
findings.description:
The SC at slice line 173 requires that "a worktree uses its own guide copy". Line 114 allows "with `--project` **or** a worktree checkout fixture". `--project` from the project root only proves the root's template is used. `resolveOperationPath` (`packages/cli/src/utils/worktree-overlay.ts:16-25`) picks the worktree path only when a registered worktree matches cwd (`packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts:105,111-115`). Require the fixture variant:
- cwd is a registered worktree with its own template, different from the root's.
- Assert the JSON `template` field points into the worktree.

`validate-worktree-scope.test.ts:76-80` explains why that fixture needs two worktrees.

findings.title: Copying the `validate.test.ts` setup into Task 4T won't find the real template or the real files
findings.description:
Line 107 says to follow `validate.test.ts`, which mocks `FileProjectStore` with `projectPath: '/tmp/test'`. Copied as is, the template path becomes `/tmp/test/project-documents/ai-project-guide/...`. Every real-design test on line 108 would then exit 2. The vitest cwd for the CLI package is `packages/cli`, so relative `project-documents/user/slices/...` arguments also fail preflight. And `handleError` calls `process.exit` (`packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:71`), so the exit-2 cases must spy on it, as `validate.test.ts:89` does. Spell out three things:
- The mocked `projectPath` is the repo root, resolved from `import.meta.url` and run through `realpath`.
- File arguments are absolute, or the test changes cwd to the repo root.
- `process.exit` is spied on in the exit-2 cases.

findings.title: Task 6 leaves out `pnpm typecheck`, which CI gates on
findings.description: Line 130 runs `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test`. CI also runs `pnpm typecheck` (root `package.json:11` → `pnpm -r typecheck`). Core has a separate `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json`, so type errors in the three new test files could pass Task 6 and fail CI. Add `pnpm typecheck` to line 130 and to the success line 132.

findings.title: No CHANGELOG entry, although the slice depends on a release
findings.description: The slice exists so that "once a cf release ships this command" the guide can repoint its references (slice lines 19, 162, 231). The project records user-facing commands under `## [Unreleased]`, and recent task files include that step (213 Task 24, 241, 242). Task 6 covers README but not CHANGELOG, so the release that unblocks the guide wouldn't announce `cf validate design`. Add an `Added` entry to Task 6.

findings.title: `parseFrontmatter` swallows read errors, so a read failure after preflight exits 1, not 2
findings.description: Design line 78 says every I/O failure exits 2. `parseFrontmatter` returns `{found:false}` on any error. If a file becomes unreadable between preflight and parsing, the result is a `doctype` failure with exit 1, not a `SliceDesignValidationError`. Task 3's wrapping step (line 79) only covers fs calls in the new file. It's a narrow race, but reading the file once in `sliceDesignFiles.ts` would close it. The file text is needed for headings anyway.

findings.title: `SliceDesignValidationError` isn't a `UserError`, so stderr says `Error: ...` and the JSON code is `UNKNOWN`
findings.description: `handleError` prints `Error: <msg>` for non-`UserError` errors and uses `code: 'UNKNOWN'` in JSON mode. The design doesn't specify stderr format, so this is acceptable. The implementer should just know that "nothing on stdout" holds but the message gets a prefix.

findings.title: Task 1's "no other file hard-codes the template path" conflicts with Task 3T
findings.description: Task 3T line 86 hard-codes the full template path in a test. Either build the test path from `GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH` + `SLICE_DESIGN_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH`, or limit Task 1's check to source files.

findings.title: Two exit-2 cases are only tested at the core level
findings.description: "Template has no required headings" and "non-regular file" are tested in 3T but not as CLI runs in 4T. No test anywhere covers "unreadable". They all go through the same `handleError(err, 2)` path that the 4T cases exercise. The design only names the valid-then-missing case as a must-test, so this is acceptable.

findings.title: Slice and task status are not set to `complete`
findings.description: Recent task files (241, 242) end by setting the slice design and task file to `status: complete` and updating `dateUpdated`. Task 6 doesn't. This is housekeeping, not a success-criterion gap.

findings.title: Claims about existing code match the code
findings.description:
Checked:
- `validate.ts` is 258 lines, and `registerValidateCommand` is the hook for `design`.
- The script is 168 lines.
- `GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH` is at `packages/core/src/guides/types.ts:313`.
- `guides/index.ts` lists names explicitly, so Task 1's "add it there" branch applies.
- The `frontmatterSchema.js` exports are at `packages/core/src/index.ts:30-39` and the `frontmatterFileValidator.js` exports at `packages/core/src/node.ts:22-29`.
- The `resolveProjectWorktree`/`resolveOperationPath` paths and `parseFrontmatter(filePath)` are as described.
- README has only the `cf validate` row (`README.md:355`).
- The guide is a tarball install tracked in git (`.gitmodules` is empty), so CI has the real template.
- Adding a subcommand doesn't break `validate.test.ts` or `help.test.ts`.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage and proportionality
findings.description:
Each criterion maps to a task:
- PASS for real designs: 4T, plus the Task 5 sweep.
- `missing:` lines: 3T and 4T.
- `docType`: 3T and 4T.
- Order and continuation: 3T and 4T.
- Exit-2 matrix, including valid-before-missing: 3T and 4T.
- JSON: 4T.
- Worktree template: 4T.
- Unit normalization: 2T.
- Real-template test: 3T.
- Build, lint and size: Task 6.

The integration requirement is handled by the post-release message on line 31. Nothing is out of scope. The size fits the slice: 3 source files, 3 test files, and no test cases beyond what the design asks for. There's no NFR, so no load test or CI-gating task is needed. The plan leaves no stuck states: the command only reads, and Task 0 handles an existing branch.
